title: Enterprise Password Management: Vaults, Sharing, and Recovery
description: A practical enterprise password management guide covering vault design, secure sharing, access lifecycle, MFA, recovery, administration, and migration from legacy stores.
author: PilotStack Editorial Team

sections.title: Inventory Credential Types and Users
sections.body: Begin by identifying the credentials the organization manages: employee logins, shared service accounts, infrastructure secrets, emergency access, and credentials owned by vendors or contractors. Different secrets have different rotation, auditing, and access needs. Map the teams that create, approve, use, and revoke them. Identify existing storage locations such as spreadsheets, browser stores, chat messages, and scripts. Do not copy every old credential into a new vault without reviewing whether it is still needed and who should own it.

sections.title: Design Vaults and Sharing Rules
sections.body: Organize vaults around clear ownership and access boundaries, not just departments or convenience. Decide which credentials may be shared, which should be assigned to an individual, and which belong in a dedicated secrets-management system rather than a human password manager. Limit sharing to the smallest group that needs access and document how emergency access is approved. Test what a user can view, copy, export, or share from each role. Avoid broad shared vaults that make offboarding and auditing difficult.

sections.title: Require Strong Authentication and Recovery
sections.body: Validate the controls that protect access to the vault itself.
items: MFA requirements are defined for ordinary and privileged users.
Recovery methods do not silently bypass the intended security level.
Emergency access has an owner, monitoring, and periodic tests.
Lost devices and suspected account compromise have documented response steps.
Administrative actions and access changes are logged where supported.
Former users and contractors lose access promptly, including shared vaults.

sections.title: Plan Onboarding, Offboarding, and Rotation
sections.body: Connect account provisioning to the organization's identity lifecycle where possible. Define who approves access to sensitive vaults and how role changes trigger permission review. When a person leaves, remove their access and rotate shared credentials they may have known, according to risk. Keep service-account ownership explicit and schedule rotation for high-impact secrets. A vault can securely store a weak or stale password; it does not automatically make the credential safe. Pair password management with MFA, least privilege, and removal of unused accounts.

sections.title: Migrate Without Spreading Secrets
sections.body: Inventory existing stores, identify duplicates and obsolete entries, and plan a controlled export/import process. Treat exports as sensitive files: restrict access, avoid sending them through email or chat, and securely remove temporary copies after validation. Test field mapping, shared items, attachments, and permissions with a small sample. Verify that users can retrieve the credentials they need and that access boundaries survived migration. Rotate credentials that were exposed in the migration process or that have unclear history.

sections.title: Administration, Audit, and Recovery
sections.body: Define who manages users, vault policies, recovery, billing, and security settings. Keep at least two trusted administrators and test recovery when one is unavailable. Review audit logs for unusual access, mass exports, permission changes, and disabled security controls. Confirm how data can be exported for backup or exit and what the vendor can recover after accidental deletion. Document service dependencies and the response plan if the password manager is unavailable during an incident.

sections.title: Evaluate Cost and Adoption
sections.body: Compare pricing and plan limits for the expected user count, external collaborators, SSO, advanced reporting, recovery, and support. Include rollout, training, migration, and ongoing administration. Measure adoption by the reduction of credentials stored in unsafe locations, successful offboarding, completion of access reviews, and fewer shared-password workarounds. Provide short guidance that helps users create unique credentials and report suspicious requests. Reassess vault structure and permissions as the organization changes.
